decisions.headline: Since 2026-10-13, iOS checkout in Paris and Madrid has failed about 3 times in 5 (checkout-to-order fell from about 62% to 24.1% in all four lines, while Android and desktop stayed at about 62%), costing about €1.33M a month in revenue, which makes it by far the biggest problem we can fix and an engineering fix rather than a marketing one.

data_sufficiency.explanation: Solid where it counts most. I checked the iOS checkout failure myself in sales_daily: Paris 5,782 orders from 24,030 iOS checkouts and Madrid 3,833 from 15,875, both 24.1%, against about 62% before and on other devices, with London as a control. The Paris Gifts sell-out (stock_events, products) and the October budget overspend (budgets vs ad_daily) are also checked. The budget-split model is only directional. It fits well (r2 ", "u22650.7) in 23 of 44 market-lines, but only 15 of those have a full history. S\u00e3o Paulo and Miami fits look overfitted, and Mexico City has no model. Gross margin wasn't available, so the uplifts are revenue figures, not profit. Comments can't be tied to single products. November pacing rests on 1 day.

findings.title: iOS checkout/payment failure in Paris and Madrid since 2026-10-13
findings.evidence: Checked in sales_daily over the 20 days since 10-13 vs the 20 days before. iOS: Paris 24,030 checkouts → 24.1% (was 62.1%), Madrid 15,875 → 24.1% (was 61.9%). Android and desktop are 61.5–62.3% in both cities, and London iOS is 61.8%. Payment-failure comments are 9.0% in Paris (20 of 222) and 7.2% in Madrid (16 of 222) vs about 2.2% elsewhere. Lost revenue is about €1.33M/month. MER fell to 7.06 in Paris and 5.70 in Madrid (last year 9.05 and 7.02).

findings.title: Paris Gifts sold out going into the gifting peak
findings.evidence: PAR-GFT-E10 has capacity 358 vs 11,053 for earlier editions. It sold out on 10-23, yet 867 units are recorded (a data or backorder anomaly). Units per day fell from 81.6 to 47.75, and line revenue per day from €15,737 to €9,771. The next edition launches 30 Nov. Last year Gifts revenue per day rose from €157k in October to €220k in November across established markets. At stake: about €67k/month at product level, €179k/month at line level.

findings.title: Google brand search and Meta retargeting are saturated; YouTube, TikTok and creators are under-funded
findings.evidence: Model's return on the next euro: Google brand €0.02–0.87 (€408.5k spent in 28 days), Meta retargeting mostly below 1 (its platform claims ROAS 3.47 vs 1.59 in our own last-click data). YouTube €2.41–9.98, TikTok €1.72–7.54, creators €1.42–7.52. A within-line shift is worth about €179k/month on the 5 best-fitting full-history lines, and up to €644k/month for the 19 lines the planner could read (that version breaks the model's own channel limits, so treat it as an upper bound).

findings.title: Beauty earns the least per extra euro; New York Home earns among the most and captures less demand than Home peers
findings.evidence: Return on the next euro: Amsterdam Beauty 0.79 (€13.4k/week) vs New York Home 2.73 (€24.1k/week, model fit r2 0.726). New York Home captures 20.1 orders per 1k searches vs a Home peer median of about 21.6. Madrid Beauty's 0.98 is left alone because the iOS fault distorts it and the fit is poor (r2 0.32).

findings.title: Rain lifts Gifts and Home demand
findings.evidence: Measured over 434 days of weather, with 95% ranges excluding zero: London Gifts +32.7% [29.3, 36.2], Milan Gifts +31.8% [28.3, 35.4], Amsterdam Gifts +27.8%, Home +12–19% in every market. Fashion drops falls 4–9% on rainy days. The 14-day forecast adds about €0.37M of rain-driven demand.

findings.title: Berlin late deliveries are hurting retention
findings.evidence: delivery_late is 62 of 224 comments (27.7%) vs 5.6% elsewhere, up since week 40. NPS fell from -10 to -48. Repeat share is 8.36% vs 11.79% the previous 4 weeks and a peer range of 11.8–12.6%. Revenue per day (€53.7k) is still at last year's level, so the damage is to future retention.

findings.title: Budget pacing: London overspent, Mexico City and Miami underspent
findings.evidence: October: London €426.5k vs €360k (+18.5%), Milan €274.2k vs €252k. Mexico City €134.6k vs €260k and Miami €196.1k vs €264k, €193k unspent together.

findings.title: Miami doesn't convert like peers; customers doubt the brand is legitimate
findings.evidence: trust_brand is 33 of 228 comments (14.5%) vs 2.9% elsewhere. CPA €27.09 vs peers €20.7–21.7. Revenue per day is 44% of São Paulo's at the same age. Session conversion is 3.23% on about 17.7k sessions a day. Next-euro return is low (Beauty 1.00), so more spend alone won't fix it.

findings.title: Not problems: seasonal or expected
findings.evidence: Amsterdam's October dip (search −17–23%) is seasonal: the same dip happened in 2025 and Amsterdam is flat on last year. Mexico City is 8 weeks into its ramp-up. Lisbon is small but captures the most demand of any market. Fashion drops softening in November is seasonal. Milan's site-navigation complaints show no conversion effect: checkout-to-order is 62.2%.

recommendations.action: Open a P0 ticket with engineering/payments to fix the iOS checkout/payment failure in Paris and Madrid, live since 2026-10-13.
recommendations.why: iOS checkout-to-order is 24.1% vs about 62% before, on Android and desktop, and in London. All 4 lines are hit; it started the same day in both cities; customers report card declines and failed payments on mobile. Marketing can't fix it, and every paid euro sending iOS traffic there is partly wasted.
recommendations.expected_impact: Recover about €1.33M/month of revenue: about €0.80M in Paris and €0.53M in Madrid.
recommendations.how_to_measure: iOS checkout-to-order for Paris and Madrid over the last 7 days should return to about 62%.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT 1.0*SUM(orders)/SUM(checkouts) AS value FROM sales_daily WHERE market IN ('Paris','Madrid') AND device='ios' AND day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM sales_daily),'-7 days')

execution.note: P0, markets Paris and Madrid. Since 2026-10-13, iOS checkout-to-order has been 24.1% (Paris 5,782 orders / 24,030 checkouts; Madrid 3,833 / 15,875) vs 62% before. Android and desktop are normal at 61.5–62.3%, and London iOS is normal at 61.8%. All 4 product lines are affected. Comments mention card declines, payment failing on phones and a frozen payment page (Paris 20 of 222, Madrid 16 of 222). Check the release, iOS payment SDK, 3DS and Apple Pay configuration shipped 10-12/13 for FR/ES and roll back if possible. Use Android as the control. About €1.33M/month of revenue is being lost.

recommendations.action: Apply the marketing-mix model's channel split across the portfolio, each line's total unchanged and no channel moved by more than 30%: away from Google brand and Meta retargeting, towards YouTube, TikTok and creators.
recommendations.why: The model fits well in 23 of 44 market-lines, and the pattern is the same everywhere: the next euro returns €0.02–0.87 on Google brand vs €2.4–10 on YouTube, TikTok and creators. One portfolio decision with a cap beats hand-picking a few lines.
recommendations.expected_impact: About +€179k/month in revenue from the well-fitted full-history lines, up to about €644k/month at the planner's upper bound. The 30% cap keeps it below the model's ceiling, and spend stays the same.
recommendations.how_to_measure: Portfolio MER (revenue / ad spend) over the last 28 days vs about the current level; also check each line's revenue against forecast.
recommendations.metric_sql: SELECT (SELECT SUM(revenue) FROM sales_daily WHERE day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM sales_daily),'-28 days')) / (SELECT SUM(spend) FROM ad_daily WHERE day > date((SELECT MAX(day) FROM ad_daily),'-28 days')) AS value

execution.note: Leadership approval. Apply the within-line reallocation, each channel moved at most ±30%. Exclude lines where the model fits poorly (r2<0.5: Paris Fashion drops/Beauty, Madrid Fashion drops/Beauty, Milan Fashion drops, Berlin Beauty) and Mexico City (no model). In São Paulo and Miami (likely overfitted) treat it as a test. Re-check in 4 weeks before going beyond 30%.

recommendations.action: Ticket to ops/logistics: restock Paris Gifts now. Bring forward the next edition (due 30 Nov, capacity 11,053) or add stock to the current one, and resolve the 358-capacity vs 867-units anomaly.
recommendations.why: PAR-GFT-E10 sold out on 10-23. Paris Gifts revenue per day fell from €15,737 to €9,771 (last year €26,511), right before the November–December gifting peak (last year +40% in November).

recommendations.why: London spend rose 6.8% while paid revenue rose 0.7%, so the extra spend bought almost nothing. The unspent new-market money should either be released deliberately or moved to the lines with the best return on the next euro.
recommendations.expected_impact: Avoids about €66k/month of low-return overspend in London and puts €193k of budget to a deliberate use.

You need to decide on #2: whether to apply the marketing-mix model's channel split across the portfolio. Spend would move away from Google brand and Meta retargeting and towards YouTube, TikTok and creators. Each line keeps its total budget and no channel moves by more than 30%. This is the only high-risk item this week. The other 10 items have been sent to their owners, starting with a P0 ticket for the iOS fix (#1).

input.brief: Data runs to 2026-11-01. Compare the 12 cities x 4 product lines on revenue, gross profit, CAC/ROAS, conversion, and share of potential demand captured (vs market_profile / search_interest). Identify market-lines that capture much less potential demand than peers, and flag ads/channels far above target CPA or showing fatigue (CTR decay, frequency). Give numbers with n, last 4 weeks vs previous 4 weeks, and the € per month at stake for each issue.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. Analyse demand drivers per market-line: weather effect (rain etc., measured with confidence), holidays, search interest trends, seasonality. Tell me which market-lines have a clearly positive measured weather effect (and which do not), upcoming holidays/seasonal peaks in the next 4-6 weeks, and stock-outs or stock risks (stock_events, product_daily) that are losing revenue — with € lost per month and the market named. Separate real signal from seasonal noise.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. Analyse voc_items/voc_labels: top complaint themes by market and product, trend over last 4 weeks vs prior, and link to conversion/returns/revenue where possible. Flag problems marketing cannot fix (product defects, delivery/logistics, checkout/site bugs) with market, product_id, n of mentions and estimated € impact, so I can route tickets to the right team. Also note any products whose demand/praise suggests a lifecycle email opportunity.

Data runs to 2026-11-01. ~€3.3M/month marketing. Fit/report your marketing-mix model per market-line: fit quality (R2/MAPE) per line, marginal ROAS per channel, recommended channel split with each line's total unchanged. Tell me in how many market-lines the fit is good, and the expected revenue/GP uplift of applying the split portfolio-wide with a per-channel cap (suggest the cap). Also identify lines with high marginal ROAS that are underfunded vs low-marginal lines that could fund them, and budget pacing issues (v_budget_pacing) vs plan.

input.sql: SELECT name, sql FROM sqlite_master WHERE name IN ('sales_daily','ad_daily','stock_events','product_daily','v_budget_pacing','budgets')

SELECT * FROM products LIMIT 3
SELECT s.product_id, s.day, s.event, p.capacity, p.end_day FROM stock_events s JOIN products p USING(product_id) WHERE s.day > '2026-09-01' ORDER BY s.day

findings.title: iOS checkout/payment failure in Paris and Madrid since 2026-10-13
findings.evidence: Checked in sales_daily over the 20 days since 10-13 vs the 20 days before. iOS: Paris 24,030 checkouts → 24.1% (was 62.1%), Madrid 15,875 → 24.1% (was 61.9%). Android and desktop are 61.5–62.3% in both cities, and London iOS is 61.8%. Payment-failure comments are 9.0% in Paris (20 of 222) and 7.2% in Madrid (16 of 222) vs about 2.2% elsewhere. Lost revenue is about €1.33M/month. MER fell to 7.06 in Paris and 5.70 in Madrid (last year 9.05 and 7.02).

findings.title: Paris Gifts sold out going into the gifting peak
findings.evidence: PAR-GFT-E10 has capacity 358 vs 11,053 for earlier editions. It sold out on 10-23, yet 867 units are recorded (a data or backorder anomaly). Units per day fell from 81.6 to 47.75, and line revenue per day from €15,737 to €9,771. The next edition launches 30 Nov. Last year Gifts revenue per day rose from €157k in October to €220k in November across established markets. At stake: about €67k/month at product level, €179k/month at line level.

findings.title: Google brand search and Meta retargeting are saturated; YouTube, TikTok and creators are under-funded
findings.evidence: Model's return on the next euro: Google brand €0.02–0.87 (€408.5k spent in 28 days), Meta retargeting mostly below 1 (its platform claims ROAS 3.47 vs 1.59 in our own last-click data). YouTube €2.41–9.98, TikTok €1.72–7.54, creators €1.42–7.52. A within-line shift is worth about €179k/month on the 5 best-fitting full-history lines, and up to €644k/month for the 19 lines the planner could read (that version breaks the model's own channel limits, so treat it as an upper bound).

findings.title: Beauty earns the least per extra euro; New York Home earns among the most and captures less demand than Home peers
findings.evidence: Return on the next euro: Amsterdam Beauty 0.79 (€13.4k/week) vs New York Home 2.73 (€24.1k/week, model fit r2 0.726). New York Home captures 20.1 orders per 1k searches vs a Home peer median of about 21.6. Madrid Beauty's 0.98 is left alone because the iOS fault distorts it and the fit is poor (r2 0.32).

findings.title: Rain lifts Gifts and Home demand
findings.evidence: Measured over 434 days of weather, with 95% ranges excluding zero: London Gifts +32.7% [29.3, 36.2], Milan Gifts +31.8% [28.3, 35.4], Amsterdam Gifts +27.8%, Home +12–19% in every market. Fashion drops falls 4–9% on rainy days. The 14-day forecast adds about €0.37M of rain-driven demand.

findings.title: Berlin late deliveries are hurting retention
findings.evidence: delivery_late is 62 of 224 comments (27.7%) vs 5.6% elsewhere, up since week 40. NPS fell from -10 to -48. findings.title: Budget pacing: London overspent, Mexico City and Miami underspent

findings.title: Miami doesn't convert like peers; customers doubt the brand is legitimate
findings.evidence: trust_brand is 33 of 228 comments (14.5%) vs 2.9% elsewhere. CPA €27.09 vs peers €20.7–21.7. Revenue per day is 44% of São Paulo's at the same age. Session conversion is 3.23% on about 17.7k sessions a day. Next-euro return is low (Beauty 1.00), so more spend alone won't fix it.

findings.title: Not problems: seasonal or expected
findings.evidence: Amsterdam's October dip (search −17–23%) is seasonal: the same dip happened in 2025 and Amsterdam is flat on last year. Mexico City is 8 weeks into its ramp-up. All 4 lines are hit; it started the same day in both cities; customers report card declines and failed payments on mobile. Marketing can't fix it, and every paid euro sending iOS traffic there is partly wasted.

recommendations.expected_impact: Saves about €3.35k/week of spend for a revenue loss of about €2.6k/week. Amsterdam Beauty's MER should rise.

execution.note: Paris, Beauty. The ad is fatigued: frequency 5.4, click-through rate 0.84% (was 1.18%), CPA €50.7. Pause it and hand its budget to the other Paris Meta ads. Creative should supply fresh Beauty prospecting assets.

recommendations.why: 14.5% of Miami comments doubt the brand is legitimate (vs 2.9% elsewhere). Session conversion is 3.23%, CPA €27.09 vs peers €20.7–21.7, and revenue per day is 44% of São Paulo's at the same age. The next euro returns little there, so the fix is conversion, not spend.
recommendations.expected_impact: A 10% relative lift in conversion would be about +€100k/month of Miami revenue (rough estimate, low confidence).

execution.note: Miami only. Version B adds trust signals above the fold: star rating and review count, press mentions, a free-returns/money-back guarantee and secure-payment badges. input.summary: The biggest issue: since 2026-10-13, iOS checkout-to-order in Madrid and Paris has fallen from about 62% to 24.1%, in all four lines. This costs about €1.3M a month in revenue and explains most of the drop in revenue, MER, CPA and demand capture in those two cities. Apart from that, the real gaps are fatigue in one Paris Beauty prospecting ad and slow ramp-up in Miami; Amsterdam's dip and Lisbon's small size are normal.

findings.title: iOS checkout broken in Madrid since 2026-10-13 (all lines)
findings.evidence: iOS checkout-to-order: last 4 weeks 35.13% vs previous 4 weeks 61.85%, same period last year 61.77%, peers 61.68–62.32%. Since 10-13: 3,833 orders from 15,875 checkouts = 24.1% over 20 days, vs 13,996/22,630 = 61.8% before. Android and desktop are normal, and all 4 lines dropped the same way. This one fault drives the market-level drops: MER 5.70 vs 7.02 last year (peers 6.45–6.86), CPA €23.84 vs €19.52, revenue per day €49.4k vs €61.7k last year. No earlier episode in the history.

findings.title: iOS checkout broken in Paris since 2026-10-13 (all lines)
findings.evidence: iOS checkout-to-order: 35.27% vs 61.63% the previous 4 weeks and 61.42% last year; peers 61.68–61.85%. Since 10-13: 5,782 orders from 24,030 checkouts = 24.1%, vs 61.6% before; average order value €58.8. Same start day as Madrid, so likely one shared release or payment change. CPA €22.41 vs €17.07 last year (peers €17.94–20.12); MER 7.06 vs 9.05; revenue per day €74.6k vs €100.0k. Paris has the lowest demand capture in Beauty, Fashion drops and Gifts (13.7–15.1 orders per 1k searches vs about 19–22 at mature peers). That gap mostly comes from this fault.

findings.title: Creative fatigue on PAR-BTY-META-PROSPECTING
findings.evidence: CTR 1.18% → 0.84% (28,285/2.41M → 20,872/2.49M impressions). That is −28.7%, p≈0 after correcting for 48 comparisons. Average frequency rose from 2.03 to 4.09 and keeps rising every day (5.21 on 10-30, with CTR at 0.63%). Spend was flat (€22.5k → €23.3k), but last-click orders fell 719 → 460, CPA rose €31.4 → €50.7 (target €25), and attributed revenue fell €29.5k → €18.9k. Part of the order loss comes from the Paris iOS fault, but the CTR decay is independent of it.

findings.title: Miami ramping slowly and capturing too little demand
findings.evidence: At week 32, revenue per day is €36.5k, 44% of São Paulo's €82.8k at the same age. Revenue per day over the last 4 weeks is €33.7k vs €30.1k the previous 4 weeks, against peers' €50.5k–53.7k. CPA is €27.09 (previous €27.85), above the €25 target and the peer range of €20.66–21.69. Demand capture is 14.5 (Beauty), 15.7 (Fashion drops), 16.4 (Gifts) and 16.2 (Home) orders per 1k searches, vs about 19–22 in mature markets. Four-week revenue across lines is about €944k. Closing the capture gap would be worth very roughly €250k a month; this is an estimate.

findings.title: Milan organic share below last year and peers
findings.evidence: Organic share 39.61% vs 42.69% the previous 4 weeks and 44.75% last year; peer range 44.62–45.01%. Not broken down by line yet.

findings.title: Berlin repeat share falling
findings.evidence: Repeat share 8.36% vs 11.79% the previous 4 weeks and 12.57% last year; peer range 11.83–12.60%. Not broken down by line yet; check the email/SMS sends and the retention flows.

proposed_actions.action: Raise a P0 on the iOS checkout/payment step for Madrid and Paris: compare the 10-12 and 10-13 releases, payment provider and Apple Pay config, and roll back if possible. Until it is fixed, cap spend on iOS placements in both cities.
proposed_actions.why: About €1.3M a month of revenue is being lost. The drop is sudden (about 62% → 24%), started on the same day in both cities, and affects only iOS.

proposed_actions.action: Rotate new creatives into PAR-BTY-META-PROSPECTING and cap frequency at about 2.5, or widen the audience.
proposed_actions.why: Frequency has doubled to 4–5, CTR is down 29%, and CPA (€50.7) is twice the €25 target.

proposed_actions.action: For Miami, review the bids on affiliates and retargeting and how prospecting is split across lines, starting with Beauty. Track demand capture against São Paulo's ramp-up.
proposed_actions.why: Miami is at 44% of the earlier launch at the same age, and its CPA is above target.

proposed_actions.action: Break down Milan organic share and Berlin repeat share by line and channel.
proposed_actions.why: Both sit outside the peer range and below last year; the money at stake isn't sized yet.

proposed_actions.action: Re-run the CPA, MER and demand-capture benchmarks for Madrid and Paris after the iOS fix.
proposed_actions.why: Their ad CPAs and demand capture can't be read reliably while the fault lasts.

not_problems: Amsterdam: revenue per day is €35.2k vs €35.9k last year, MER 4.84 vs 4.93 and CPA €26.04 vs €25.96. The drop from the previous 4 weeks (€44.6k) is a seasonal dip that happens every year. Amsterdam's MER is still structurally below the target of 8.

input.summary: The biggest problem that needs action is in Paris Gifts. Edition 11 (capacity 358) sold out on 23 Oct. Product sales fell from 81.6 to 47.75 units a day afterwards, and line revenue per day dropped to €9,771, against €15,737 the period before and €26,511 a year earlier. The replacement edition doesn't launch until 30 Nov, so the gap runs straight into the gifting peak. Last year Gifts revenue per day in established markets went from €157k in October to €220k in November and €302k for 1–24 December. Rain clearly lifts Home and Gifts nearly everywhere and hurts Fashion drops. The demand model is reliable (holdout MAPE 8%), and most other apparent dips, including Amsterdam's October search drop, also happened last year.

findings.title: Stock-out: Paris Gifts Edition 11 sold out 23 Oct and line revenue fell sharply going into the gifting peak
findings.evidence: stock_events shows PAR-GFT-E10 'sold_out' on 2026-10-23. Its capacity is 358 against 11,053 for every earlier edition. Units averaged 81.6 a day in days 1–5 and 47.75 a day in days 6–13. Earlier editions held steady between those two windows (e.g. E09 115.6 → 132, E06 147 → 150). Paris Gifts revenue per day for 24 Oct–1 Nov was €9,771, against €15,737 the previous period and €26,511 the same period last year. Peer median is €20,026 (range €13,146–26,906), so Paris is outside the peer range. The product-level loss alone is about 34 units/day × €66 ≈ €2.2k/day (~€67k/month). The line-level drop against the previous period is about €6.0k/day (~€179k/month). The edition runs to 29 Nov, and the next one (E11, capacity 11,053) only starts 30 Nov. Data oddity: product_daily records 867 units sold against a capacity of 358 (backorders or a data issue). Handing off to the stock/ops specialist.

findings.title: Rain has a clearly positive measured effect on Home and Gifts; Fashion drops is consistently negative
findings.evidence: Over 434 days of real weather, the 95% range excludes zero for Home in every market measured (e.g. Milan +18.8% [16.0, 21.7], Paris +16.6%, London +16.5%, NY +16.1%, Madrid +15.8%, Miami +12.3% [4.3, 20.8]). The same holds for Gifts in every market except Miami. The strongest Gifts effects are London +32.7% [29.3, 36.2], Milan +31.8% [28.3, 35.4] and Amsterdam +27.8% [24.2, 31.5], with São Paulo at +19.2%. Beauty has small positive effects in Paris (+5.9), Berlin (+5.6), NY (+3.9), London (+3.7) and Barcelona (+3.4). Beauty shows no clear effect (range includes zero) in Madrid, Lisbon, Milan, Amsterdam, São Paulo and Miami, and neither does Miami Gifts [-0.8, 16.4]. Fashion drops falls with rain everywhere, by -4% to -9%. Mexico City has no weather estimate.

findings.title: 14-day forecast: rain-driven uplift worth about €0.4M, mostly Gifts and Home
findings.market: São Paulo, London, Milan, Barcelona, Paris, NY, Madrid
findings.evidence: demand_outlook for 2–15 Nov: São Paulo Gifts +13.0% (+€41.5k, 8 rainy days), São Paulo Home +9.7% (+€36.9k), London Gifts +5.6% (+€21.1k), Milan Gifts +10.7% (+€19.6k), Barcelona Home +7.4% (+€18.6k), Paris Home +€17.2k, NY Home +€17.1k, Madrid Home +€16.1k, and smaller amounts elsewhere. The listed cells add up to about €0.37M. Model holdout MAPE is 8.0%, with 81% of predictions within 10%, so these uplifts are only slightly larger than the model's typical error.

findings.title: Holiday and seasonal peaks over the next 4–6 weeks
findings.evidence: Public holidays coming up: 11 Nov in France and the US, 15 and 20 Nov in Brazil, 16 Nov in Mexico, 26 Nov US Thanksgiving, 1 Dec Portugal, 6 and 8 Dec in Spain, Italy and Portugal. The biggest measured holiday effects are Madrid Home +21.2%, London Gifts +19.7%, Berlin Home +16.9%, Madrid Gifts +16.1%, Miami Home +15.2%, London Home +14.2% and São Paulo Gifts +13.9%. Holidays have little or a negative effect on Fashion drops and Beauty. For seasonality, last year in established markets Gifts revenue per day went €157k (Oct) → €220k (Nov) → €302k (1–24 Dec). Home went €189k → €224k → €251k and Beauty €121k → €124k → €154k. Fashion drops was flat to slightly down (€168k → €157k → €154k).

findings.title: New markets are under-capturing demand: Miami and Mexico City at 69–76% of peer capture
findings.evidence: Measured over 8 weeks. Miami: Home 74% (gap €205k), Fashion drops 76% (€169k), Beauty 69% (€167k), Gifts 74% (€159k). Mexico City: Home 72% (€177k), Fashion drops 75% (€135k), Gifts 75% (€118k), Beauty 72% (€100k). Mexico City searches rose 2.3–2.5× in the last 4 weeks compared with the 4 before. Some of this gap is expected while a market is still ramping up. Miami's marginal ROAS is weak to moderate (Home 1.84, Beauty 1.00), so more spend alone won't close it.

findings.title: Established-market capture gaps: Paris (all lines) and Amsterdam Gifts
findings.evidence: Paris capture over the last 8 weeks: Fashion drops 88% (gap €203k), Gifts 86% (€199k, partly caused by the stock-out), Home 90% (€178k), Beauty 88% (€140k). Paris Home and Fashion drops still have room to spend more efficiently: marginal ROAS 2.32 and 2.22, best channels YouTube 6.8 and TikTok 4.77. That points to a reach/budget gap. Paris Beauty has a marginal ROAS of only 1.35, so its gap is not a budget gap. Amsterdam Gifts captures 78% (gap €235k over 8 weeks) with marginal ROAS 1.83, but its revenue per day of €13,483 is in line with last year (€13,745) and peers (median €12,900). Treat it as a reach gap of moderate priority.

proposed_actions.action: Restock Paris Gifts now: bring forward Edition 12 (capacity 11,053, due 30 Nov) or add stock to Edition 11, and confirm the 358 capacity and the 867 units recorded with ops.
proposed_actions.why: About €2.2k/day is being lost at product level and about €6k/day at line level, during the month when Gifts demand rose about 40% last year.

proposed_actions.action: Schedule rain-triggered budget for Gifts and Home in London, Milan, Amsterdam, São Paulo, Paris and NY, and pull back Fashion drops on rainy days.
proposed_actions.why: Rain effects are measured with ranges that exclude zero: +14–33% for Gifts and Home, and -4% to -9% for Fashion drops.

proposed_actions.action: Shift budget toward Gifts and Home ahead of 11 Nov (France, US), 26 Nov (US) and 6–8 Dec (Spain, Italy, Portugal). Favour high-return cells like NY Home (marginal ROAS 2.73), São Paulo Home (3.71) and Paris Home (2.32).
proposed_actions.why: These lines have the largest holiday effects and seasonal ramps, and spare marginal return.

proposed_actions.action: Cut spend in or move budget away from Beauty in Amsterdam (marginal ROAS 0.79), Madrid (0.98) and Miami (1.00).
proposed_actions.why: One more euro there returns about a euro or less, and those Beauty cells are not under-capturing demand except Miami.

not_problems: Amsterdam searches fell 17–23% in the last 4 weeks against the 4 before, across all lines. The same October dip happened in 2025 (Gifts went from about 105k in early September to about 64k in early October, then recovered to 136k by mid-November), so it's seasonal.
Search interest in established markets is flat year on year (0.96–1.03×), so demand hasn't shifted structurally.
Fashion drops dipping on rainy days and in November is normal: the rain effect is negative everywhere, and last year November and December ran below October.
London, Lisbon, Barcelona and NY capturing more than 100% of peer demand is not a measurement error. They are simply outperforming peers.
Low capture in Miami and Mexico City partly reflects early-stage launch ramps (both are flagged as new markets).

input.summary: The biggest problem is a broken iOS checkout in Paris and Madrid. Since 2026-10-14, iOS checkout-to-order has dropped to about 22% (it was about 62% last period, last year, on Android and in peer markets), customers are complaining about failed payments, and we are losing an estimated €0.84M a month in Paris and €0.55M a month in Madrid. Berlin has a new late-delivery problem: 28% of comments, NPS down from -10 to -48 and repeat share down to 8.4% against a peer median of 12.2%. Both need engineering and logistics fixes, not marketing.

findings.title: iOS payment/checkout failure (checkout bug, route to engineering/payments)
findings.line: all (Home strongest: payment_problem 11.7% of Home comments)
findings.evidence: payment_problem is 9.0% of Paris comments (20 of 222) vs 2.2% elsewhere and 1.1% before, p<0.001. Gist: 'card declined at checkout', 'payment fails when checking out on phone'. iOS checkout→order over 28 days is 35.3% vs 61.6% last period, 61.4% last year and a peer range of 61.7–61.9. Android is 62.1%, which is normal. It started 2026-10-14 and has run at 22.1% since. Lost revenue = iOS checkouts × (61.7% baseline − actual) × AOV €58.80: €531,906 over 19 days.

findings.title: iOS payment/checkout failure (same bug as Paris, route to engineering/payments)
findings.evidence: payment_problem is 7.2% of Madrid comments (16 of 222) vs 2.3% elsewhere and 0.8% before, p<0.001. Gist: 'card gave an error', 'payment failed several times on mobile', 'payment page froze'. iOS checkout→order is 35.1% vs 61.9% last period and 61.8% last year, peer median 62.0. Android is 61.7%, which is normal. It started the same day, 2026-10-14, and has run at 22.0% since. Lost revenue: €349,445 over 19 days at AOV €58.58. NPS is -36 (was -30).

findings.title: Late or missing deliveries (logistics, route to ops/carrier)
findings.line: all lines (Fashion drops 29.3%, Beauty 28.6%, Gifts 26.8%, Home 25.9%)
findings.evidence: delivery_late is 62 of 224 comments (27.7%) vs 5.6% elsewhere and 6.2% before, p<0.001. The weekly count was 2–7 until week 39 and has been 20/13/20/9 since week 40. Gist: 'still waiting for my order', 'arrived a week late'. NPS fell from -10 to -48. Repeat share is 8.36% vs 11.79% last period, 12.57% last year and a peer range of 11.8–12.6. Revenue/day (€53,678) is still at last year's level (€55,765), so the damage shows in retention more than in current sales. I could not compute a reliable € figure.

findings.title: Website navigation complaints, no conversion impact yet (route to UX, low priority)
findings.evidence: website_ux is 27 of 215 comments (12.6%) vs 4.0% elsewhere and 5.8% before, p<0.001. Gist: 'website confusing to navigate'. Checkout→order is 62.17%, which matches last period (61.81%), last year (62.07%) and peers. No measurable revenue effect.

findings.title: Customers don't recognise the brand and doubt it is legitimate (new market, marketing can address)
findings.evidence: trust_brand is 33 of 228 comments (14.5%) vs 2.9% elsewhere and 6.6% before. Gist: 'never heard of the brand, doubts legitimacy'. CPA is €27.09 vs a peer range of €20.7–21.7. In week 32 after launch, revenue/day is €36,509, 44% of what São Paulo had at the same age. This is a brand-awareness issue, not a defect.

proposed_actions.action: Open a P1 ticket with payments/engineering for the iOS checkout (card declines and failures) in Paris and Madrid, starting 2026-10-14. Check the iOS payment SDK/3DS or the release shipped that day. Use Android as the control.
proposed_actions.why: About €1.39M a month is being lost across both markets. Marketing can't fix it, and every euro spent on ads that sends iOS traffic there is partly wasted.

proposed_actions.action: Until the fix ships, send recovery emails/SMS to iOS users who abandoned checkout in Paris and Madrid since 2026-10-14, with a desktop or alternative-payment link.
proposed_actions.why: About 37.9k iOS checkouts across the two markets ended without an order. Some of that revenue can be won back.

proposed_actions.action: Send a ticket to ops/logistics about the Berlin carrier delays (since week 40), and send affected Berlin customers a proactive apology and delivery-status email.
proposed_actions.why: NPS fell from -10 to -48 and repeat share is 3.9 points below peers. This will keep costing retention.

proposed_actions.action: Lifecycle email: run a back-in-stock/waitlist flow for PAR-GFT-E10 (Paris · Gifts · Edition 11, €66, sold out 2026-10-23). In Amsterdam Gifts, send new-gift-range announcement emails (8 of 61 comments, 13.1%, ask for more gift options).
proposed_actions.why: There is demand we couldn't fill. praise_product is the most common theme overall (568 mentions, 21% of comments), so happy customers can be targeted for reviews and referrals.

proposed_actions.action: In Miami, add trust signals (reviews, press, guarantees) to ads and landing pages.
proposed_actions.why: Comments doubting the brand's legitimacy have doubled, and CPA is above peers.

not_problems: Comment data has no product_id, so mentions can only be tied to market × line, not to individual products. The only product-level signal is the PAR-GFT-E10 sell-out.

Across all markets, theme volumes are stable compared with the prior 28 days: praise_product 568 vs 556, price_value 327 vs 331, product_quality 189 vs 210, returns_refunds 124 vs 125. No network-wide product-defect or returns spike.
sold_out complaints fell overall (91 vs 113).
Milan's navigation complaints don't show up in conversion: checkout→order matches last year and peers.
Berlin revenue/day is in line with last year and above peers. The delivery problem shows in NPS and repeat share, not yet in current sales.
NPS improved in London (-23 to -5), Mexico City (-23 to 2), New York and Amsterdam. Barcelona and São Paulo are flat. Nothing to act on there.

input.summary: Moving spend between channels inside each line's existing budget is worth about €149k/week in revenue (≈€644k/month) for the 19 market-lines whose plans I could read. Only €41k/week (≈€179k/month) of that comes from lines where the model fits well on a full 60 weeks of data, so treat the rest as something to test, not a forecast. The pattern is the same in nearly every market-line: Google brand search and Meta retargeting bring in little extra revenue per euro (Google brand €0.02–0.87 back per €1) and can fund YouTube, TikTok and creators (€2.4–10 per €1). London overspent its October budget by €66.5k (+18.5%), and Paris and Madrid organic revenue is down about 20% on last year even though search demand is flat. That organic drop is a real problem, not seasonality.

findings.title: Portfolio channel shift inside each line: +€148.8k/week of revenue expected (19 market-lines visible)
findings.evidence: The plan's tool output was cut off after 19 of 44 market-lines. Their expected weekly gains add up to €148,820 (≈€644k/month at 4.33 weeks), or +3.8% to +7.3% per line. The 25 lines I could not see each gain ≤€5,436/week, the smallest gain shown. Only revenue can be sized; I did not pull margin data, so the gross-profit uplift is not stated. Of the €148.8k: €41.3k/week (≈€179k/month) comes from 5 lines with r2 ≥0.7 on 60 weeks: New York Home €10,714 (r2 0.726), New York Gifts €9,636 (0.909), London Gifts €8,393 (0.924), Barcelona Home €7,115 (0.754), Berlin Gifts €5,436 (0.919). €23.1k/week comes from São Paulo (r2 0.98+ but only 42 weeks). €19.3k/week comes from poor fits: Paris Beauty €7,352 (r2 0.282), Paris Fashion drops €6,299 (0.243), Milan Fashion drops €5,690 (0.362). The plan breaks its own stated ±50% channel limit, with increases of +60% to +84%, so the stated gains are probably too high.

findings.title: Model fit: good in 23 of 44 market-lines, but only 15 of those have a full history
findings.evidence: r2 ≥0.7 in 23 of 44 market-lines. Gifts is good in all 11 markets with a model (0.607 Paris, 0.851–0.944 elsewhere). Amsterdam is good in all 4 lines (0.74–0.944). São Paulo (0.983–0.989, 42 weeks) and Miami (0.989–0.992, 32 weeks) fit almost perfectly, which with 8 channels plus search as inputs on so few weeks looks like overfitting. r2 is below 0.5 in 6 lines: Paris Fashion drops 0.243, Paris Beauty 0.282, Madrid Fashion drops 0.312, Madrid Beauty 0.323, Milan Fashion drops 0.362, Berlin Beauty 0.424. Mexico City has no model (8 weeks of data). Search interest explains most of the revenue (search elasticity ≈0.95 everywhere). The all-market Meta prospecting figure (0.9524) equals that search figure, so it reflects demand and should not be trusted; per-line Meta prospecting is 0.06–0.08. Ask the model owner for MAPE: the tool reports only r2.

findings.title: Google brand search is saturated: it gets most of the last-click credit but brings in little extra revenue
findings.evidence: Last 28 days: €408,524 spent. Our own last-click data says 9.48 ROAS and the platform claims 10.4, but the model's return on the next euro is only 0.02 (Paris Gifts) to 0.87 (São Paulo Home). Most lines are below 0.5, for example London Home 0.13, Barcelona Beauty 0.06 and Amsterdam Fashion drops 0.03. The plan cuts brand search by 39–47% in every line it shows.

findings.title: Meta retargeting: platform claims about twice what our own data shows, and the model says it adds little
findings.evidence: Platform ROAS 3.47 against 1.59 from our own last-click data (€1.22M claimed vs €559k last-click on €351k spend over 28 days). The model's return on the next euro is mostly below 1, e.g. London Beauty 0.44, Madrid Beauty 0.36, Berlin Gifts 0.46. Exceptions are São Paulo (1.63–2.11) and Paris Home (1.89). TikTok also over-claims (platform 6.04 vs our 3.38), but the model still values its next euro at 1.72–7.54.

findings.title: YouTube, TikTok and creators are under-funded in every market
findings.evidence: YouTube's return on the next euro is 2.41–9.98 on only €611–1,559/week per line (London Home 8.09, New York Home 8.72, São Paulo Home 9.98). TikTok is 1.72–7.54 and creators 1.42–7.52. Our last-click data undercounts YouTube (2.98 ROAS vs the platform's 5.73), as expected for upper-funnel video.

findings.title: Moving budget between lines: Beauty earns least per extra euro, Home and New York/São Paulo lines earn most
findings.evidence: Blended return on the next euro, top lines: São Paulo Home 3.71, New York Home 2.73, São Paulo Fashion drops 2.73, São Paulo Gifts 2.72, New York Fashion drops 2.51, London Home 2.43, Paris Home 2.32. Bottom: Amsterdam Beauty 0.79 (€13,386/week), Madrid Beauty 0.98 (€15,253/week), Miami Beauty 1.00, Amsterdam Fashion drops 1.05, Lisbon Beauty 1.09, Milan Beauty 1.12. These are marginal returns at the current spend level, so large moves should be stepped and re-checked.

findings.title: London overspent its October budget by €66.5k (+18.5%); Milan by €22k
findings.evidence: October spend €426,549 against a €360,000 budget; September was on plan at €357,657. Milan spent €274,205 against €252,000 (+8.8%). Organic-vs-paid shows London's 28-day spend up 6.8% while paid revenue rose only 0.7%. November pacing (projected at 90.9%) rests on 1 day of data and is not yet meaningful.

findings.title: Organic revenue in Paris and Madrid is down about 20% on last year while search demand is flat
findings.evidence: Organic revenue vs last year: Paris −24.3% and Madrid −20.2%, with spend roughly flat (−2.0% and −1.7%). Search interest over the last 4 weeks vs last year: Paris +0.3%, Madrid −0.4%. So falling demand does not explain it; the cause is likely conversion, site or stock problems. Milan organic is −18.2% on last year with search −2.5%.

findings.title: Mexico City and Miami are well under budget

output.summary: The biggest issue: since 2026-10-13, iOS checkout-to-order in Madrid and Paris has fallen from about 62% to 24.1%, in all four lines. This costs about €1.3M a month in revenue and explains most of the drop in revenue, MER, CPA and demand capture in those two cities. Apart from that, the real gaps are fatigue in one Paris Beauty prospecting ad and slow ramp-up in Miami; Amsterdam's dip and Lisbon's small size are normal.

findings.title: iOS checkout broken in Madrid since 2026-10-13 (all lines)
findings.evidence: iOS checkout-to-order: last 4 weeks 35.13% vs previous 4 weeks 61.85%, same period last year 61.77%, peers 61.68–62.32%. Since 10-13: 3,833 orders from 15,875 checkouts = 24.1% over 20 days, vs 13,996/22,630 = 61.8% before. Android and desktop are normal, and all 4 lines dropped the same way. This one fault drives the market-level drops: MER 5.70 vs 7.02 last year (peers 6.45–6.86), CPA €23.84 vs €19.52, revenue per day €49.4k vs €61.7k last year. No earlier episode in the history.

findings.title: iOS checkout broken in Paris since 2026-10-13 (all lines)
findings.evidence: iOS checkout-to-order: 35.27% vs 61.63% the previous 4 weeks and 61.42% last year; peers 61.68–61.85%. Since 10-13: 5,782 orders from 24,030 checkouts = 24.1%, vs 61.6% before; average order value €58.8. Same start day as Madrid, so likely one shared release or payment change. CPA €22.41 vs €17.07 last year (peers €17.94–20.12); MER 7.06 vs 9.05; revenue per day €74.6k vs €100.0k. Paris has the lowest demand capture in Beauty, Fashion drops and Gifts (13.7–15.1 orders per 1k searches vs about 19–22 at mature peers). That gap mostly comes from this fault.

findings.title: Creative fatigue on PAR-BTY-META-PROSPECTING
findings.evidence: CTR 1.18% → 0.84% (28,285/2.41M → 20,872/2.49M impressions). That is −28.7%, p≈0 after correcting for 48 comparisons. Average frequency rose from 2.03 to 4.09 and keeps rising every day (5.21 on 10-30, with CTR at 0.63%). Spend was flat (€22.5k → €23.3k), but last-click orders fell 719 → 460, CPA rose €31.4 → €50.7 (target €25), and attributed revenue fell €29.5k → €18.9k. Part of the order loss comes from the Paris iOS fault, but the CTR decay is independent of it.

findings.title: Miami ramping slowly and capturing too little demand
findings.evidence: At week 32, revenue per day is €36.5k, 44% of São Paulo's €82.8k at the same age. Revenue per day over the last 4 weeks is €33.7k vs €30.1k the previous 4 weeks, against peers' €50.5k–53.7k. CPA is €27.09 (previous €27.85), above the €25 target and the peer range of €20.66–21.69. Demand capture is 14.5 (Beauty), 15.7 (Fashion drops), 16.4 (Gifts) and 16.2 (Home) orders per 1k searches, vs about 19–22 in mature markets. Four-week revenue across lines is about €944k. Closing the capture gap would be worth very roughly €250k a month; this is an estimate.

findings.title: Milan organic share below last year and peers
findings.evidence: Organic share 39.61% vs 42.69% the previous 4 weeks and 44.75% last year; peer range 44.62–45.01%. Not broken down by line yet.

findings.title: Berlin repeat share falling
findings.evidence: Repeat share 8.36% vs 11.79% the previous 4 weeks and 12.57% last year; peer range 11.83–12.60%. Not broken down by line yet; check the email/SMS sends and the retention flows.

proposed_actions.action: Raise a P0 on the iOS checkout/payment step for Madrid and Paris: compare the 10-12 and 10-13 releases, payment provider and Apple Pay config, and roll back if possible. Until it is fixed, cap spend on iOS placements in both cities.
proposed_actions.why: About €1.3M a month of revenue is being lost. The drop is sudden (about 62% → 24%), started on the same day in both cities, and affects only iOS.

proposed_actions.action: Rotate new creatives into PAR-BTY-META-PROSPECTING and cap frequency at about 2.5, or widen the audience.
proposed_actions.why: Frequency has doubled to 4–5, CTR is down 29%, and CPA (€50.7) is twice the €25 target.

proposed_actions.action: For Miami, review the bids on affiliates and retargeting and how prospecting is split across lines, starting with Beauty. Track demand capture against São Paulo's ramp-up.
proposed_actions.why: Miami is at 44% of the earlier launch at the same age, and its CPA is above target.

proposed_actions.action: Break down Milan organic share and Berlin repeat share by line and channel.
proposed_actions.why: Both sit outside the peer range and below last year; the money at stake isn't sized yet.

proposed_actions.action: Re-run the CPA, MER and demand-capture benchmarks for Madrid and Paris after the iOS fix.
proposed_actions.why: Their ad CPAs and demand capture can't be read reliably while the fault lasts.

not_problems: Amsterdam: revenue per day is €35.2k vs €35.9k last year, MER 4.84 vs 4.93 and CPA €26.04 vs €25.96. The drop from the previous 4 weeks (€44.6k) is a seasonal dip that happens every year. Amsterdam's MER is still structurally below the target of 8.

Lisbon: revenue is low compared with peers (€35.4k vs €50.5k–53.7k per day) but flat against last year (€36.1k). Lisbon captures the most demand of any market (20.9–24.8 orders per 1k searches); it is simply a smaller, less affluent market (2.9M people, affluence 0.85).

Mexico City: only 8 weeks old and ramping fast (€13.9k → €38.4k per day). Comparing it with mature peers is unfair, and its CPAs are falling across ads (e.g. Meta prospecting for Gifts €89.1 → €53.4).

High ad-level CPAs on affiliates and retargeting (about €50–90) are last-click views that show up in every market and are stable from period to period. They can't be compared directly with the blended CPA target.
No market is out of line on paid share, Android checkout or desktop checkout.

output.summary: The biggest problem that needs action is in Paris Gifts. Edition 11 (capacity 358) sold out on 23 Oct. Product sales fell from 81.6 to 47.75 units a day afterwards, and line revenue per day dropped to €9,771, against €15,737 the period before and €26,511 a year earlier. The replacement edition doesn't launch until 30 Nov, so the gap runs straight into the gifting peak. Last year Gifts revenue per day in established markets went from €157k in October to €220k in November and €302k for 1–24 December. Rain clearly lifts Home and Gifts nearly everywhere and hurts Fashion drops. The demand model is reliable (holdout MAPE 8%), and most other apparent dips, including Amsterdam's October search drop, also happened last year.

findings.title: Stock-out: Paris Gifts Edition 11 sold out 23 Oct and line revenue fell sharply going into the gifting peak
findings.evidence: stock_events shows PAR-GFT-E10 'sold_out' on 2026-10-23. Its capacity is 358 against 11,053 for every earlier edition. Units averaged 81.6 a day in days 1–5 and 47.75 a day in days 6–13. Earlier editions held steady between those two windows (e.g. E09 115.6 → 132, E06 147 → 150). Paris Gifts revenue per day for 24 Oct–1 Nov was €9,771, against €15,737 the previous period and €26,511 the same period last year. Peer median is €20,026 (range €13,146–26,906), so Paris is outside the peer range. The product-level loss alone is about 34 units/day × €66 ≈ €2.2k/day (~€67k/month). The line-level drop against the previous period is about €6.0k/day (~€179k/month). The edition runs to 29 Nov, and the next one (E11, capacity 11,053) only starts 30 Nov. Data oddity: product_daily records 867 units sold against a capacity of 358 (backorders or a data issue). Handing off to the stock/ops specialist.

findings.title: Rain has a clearly positive measured effect on Home and Gifts; Fashion drops is consistently negative
findings.evidence: Over 434 days of real weather, the 95% range excludes zero for Home in every market measured (e.g. Milan +18.8% [16.0, 21.7], Paris +16.6%, London +16.5%, NY +16.1%, Madrid +15.8%, Miami +12.3% [4.3, 20.8]). The same holds for Gifts in every market except Miami. The strongest Gifts effects are London +32.7% [29.3, 36.2], Milan +31.8% [28.3, 35.4] and Amsterdam +27.8% [24.2, 31.5], with São Paulo at +19.2%. Beauty has small positive effects in Paris (+5.9), Berlin (+5.6), NY (+3.9), London (+3.7) and Barcelona (+3.4). Beauty shows no clear effect (range includes zero) in Madrid, Lisbon, Milan, Amsterdam, São Paulo and Miami, and neither does Miami Gifts [-0.8, 16.4]. Fashion drops falls with rain everywhere, by -4% to -9%. Mexico City has no weather estimate.

findings.title: 14-day forecast: rain-driven uplift worth about €0.4M, mostly Gifts and Home
findings.market: São Paulo, London, Milan, Barcelona, Paris, NY, Madrid
findings.evidence: demand_outlook for 2–15 Nov: São Paulo Gifts +13.0% (+€41.5k, 8 rainy days), São Paulo Home +9.7% (+€36.9k), London Gifts +5.6% (+€21.1k), Milan Gifts +10.7% (+€19.6k), Barcelona Home +7.4% (+€18.6k), Paris Home +€17.2k, NY Home +€17.1k, Madrid Home +€16.1k, and smaller amounts elsewhere. The listed cells add up to about €0.37M. Model holdout MAPE is 8.0%, with 81% of predictions within 10%, so these uplifts are only slightly larger than the model's typical error.

findings.title: Holiday and seasonal peaks over the next 4–6 weeks
findings.evidence: Public holidays coming up: 11 Nov in France and the US, 15 and 20 Nov in Brazil, 16 Nov in Mexico, 26 Nov US Thanksgiving, 1 Dec Portugal, 6 and 8 Dec in Spain, Italy and Portugal. The biggest measured holiday effects are Madrid Home +21.2%, London Gifts +19.7%, Berlin Home +16.9%, Madrid Gifts +16.1%, Miami Home +15.2%, London Home +14.2% and São Paulo Gifts +13.9%. Holidays have little or a negative effect on Fashion drops and Beauty. For seasonality, last year in established markets Gifts revenue per day went €157k (Oct) → €220k (Nov) → €302k (1–24 Dec). Home went €189k → €224k → €251k and Beauty €121k → €124k → €154k. Fashion drops was flat to slightly down (€168k → €157k → €154k).

findings.title: New markets are under-capturing demand: Miami and Mexico City at 69–76% of peer capture
findings.evidence: Measured over 8 weeks. Miami: Home 74% (gap €205k), Fashion drops 76% (€169k), Beauty 69% (€167k), Gifts 74% (€159k). Mexico City: Home 72% (€177k), Fashion drops 75% (€135k), Gifts 75% (€118k), Beauty 72% (€100k). Mexico City searches rose 2.3–2.5× in the last 4 weeks compared with the 4 before. Some of this gap is expected while a market is still ramping up. Miami's marginal ROAS is weak to moderate (Home 1.84, Beauty 1.00), so more spend alone won't close it.

findings.title: Established-market capture gaps: Paris (all lines) and Amsterdam Gifts
findings.evidence: Paris capture over the last 8 weeks: Fashion drops 88% (gap €203k), Gifts 86% (€199k, partly caused by the stock-out), Home 90% (€178k), Beauty 88% (€140k). Paris Home and Fashion drops still have room to spend more efficiently: marginal ROAS 2.32 and 2.22, best channels YouTube 6.8 and TikTok 4.77. That points to a reach/budget gap. Paris Beauty has a marginal ROAS of only 1.35, so its gap is not a budget gap. Amsterdam Gifts captures 78% (gap €235k over 8 weeks) with marginal ROAS 1.83, but its revenue per day of €13,483 is in line with last year (€13,745) and peers (median €12,900). Treat it as a reach gap of moderate priority.

proposed_actions.action: Restock Paris Gifts now: bring forward Edition 12 (capacity 11,053, due 30 Nov) or add stock to Edition 11, and confirm the 358 capacity and the 867 units recorded with ops.
proposed_actions.why: About €2.2k/day is being lost at product level and about €6k/day at line level, during the month when Gifts demand rose about 40% last year.

proposed_actions.action: Schedule rain-triggered budget for Gifts and Home in London, Milan, Amsterdam, São Paulo, Paris and NY, and pull back Fashion drops on rainy days.
proposed_actions.why: Rain effects are measured with ranges that exclude zero: +14–33% for Gifts and Home, and -4% to -9% for Fashion drops.

proposed_actions.action: Shift budget toward Gifts and Home ahead of 11 Nov (France, US), 26 Nov (US) and 6–8 Dec (Spain, Italy, Portugal). Favour high-return cells like NY Home (marginal ROAS 2.73), São Paulo Home (3.71) and Paris Home (2.32).
proposed_actions.why: These lines have the largest holiday effects and seasonal ramps, and spare marginal return.

proposed_actions.action: Cut spend in or move budget away from Beauty in Amsterdam (marginal ROAS 0.79), Madrid (0.98) and Miami (1.00).
proposed_actions.why: One more euro there returns about a euro or less, and those Beauty cells are not under-capturing demand except Miami.

not_problems: Amsterdam searches fell 17–23% in the last 4 weeks against the 4 before, across all lines. The same October dip happened in 2025 (Gifts went from about 105k in early September to about 64k in early October, then recovered to 136k by mid-November), so it's seasonal.
Search interest in established markets is flat year on year (0.96–1.03×), so demand hasn't shifted structurally.
Fashion drops dipping on rainy days and in November is normal: the rain effect is negative everywhere, and last year November and December ran below October.
London, Lisbon, Barcelona and NY capturing more than 100% of peer demand is not a measurement error. They are simply outperforming peers.
Low capture in Miami and Mexico City partly reflects early-stage launch ramps (both are flagged as new markets).

output.summary: The biggest problem is a broken iOS checkout in Paris and Madrid. Since 2026-10-14, iOS checkout-to-order has dropped to about 22% (it was about 62% last period, last year, on Android and in peer markets), customers are complaining about failed payments, and we are losing an estimated €0.84M a month in Paris and €0.55M a month in Madrid. Berlin has a new late-delivery problem: 28% of comments, NPS down from -10 to -48 and repeat share down to 8.4% against a peer median of 12.2%. Both need engineering and logistics fixes, not marketing.

findings.title: iOS payment/checkout failure (checkout bug, route to engineering/payments)
findings.line: all (Home strongest: payment_problem 11.7% of Home comments)
findings.evidence: payment_problem is 9.0% of Paris comments (20 of 222) vs 2.2% elsewhere and 1.1% before, p<0.001. Gist: 'card declined at checkout', 'payment fails when checking out on phone'. iOS checkout→order over 28 days is 35.3% vs 61.6% last period, 61.4% last year and a peer range of 61.7–61.9. Android is 62.1%, which is normal. It started 2026-10-14 and has run at 22.1% since. Lost revenue = iOS checkouts × (61.7% baseline − actual) × AOV €58.80: €531,906 over 19 days.

findings.title: iOS payment/checkout failure (same bug as Paris, route to engineering/payments)
findings.evidence: payment_problem is 7.2% of Madrid comments (16 of 222) vs 2.3% elsewhere and 0.8% before, p<0.001. Gist: 'card gave an error', 'payment failed several times on mobile', 'payment page froze'. iOS checkout→order is 35.1% vs 61.9% last period and 61.8% last year, peer median 62.0. Android is 61.7%, which is normal. It started the same day, 2026-10-14, and has run at 22.0% since. Lost revenue: €349,445 over 19 days at AOV €58.58. NPS is -36 (was -30).

findings.title: Late or missing deliveries (logistics, route to ops/carrier)
findings.line: all lines (Fashion drops 29.3%, Beauty 28.6%, Gifts 26.8%, Home 25.9%)
findings.evidence: delivery_late is 62 of 224 comments (27.7%) vs 5.6% elsewhere and 6.2% before, p<0.001. The weekly count was 2–7 until week 39 and has been 20/13/20/9 since week 40. Gist: 'still waiting for my order', 'arrived a week late'. NPS fell from -10 to -48. Repeat share is 8.36% vs 11.79% last period, 12.57% last year and a peer range of 11.8–12.6. Revenue/day (€53,678) is still at last year's level (€55,765), so the damage shows in retention more than in current sales. I could not compute a reliable € figure.

findings.title: Website navigation complaints, no conversion impact yet (route to UX, low priority)
findings.evidence: website_ux is 27 of 215 comments (12.6%) vs 4.0% elsewhere and 5.8% before, p<0.001. Gist: 'website confusing to navigate'. Checkout→order is 62.17%, which matches last period (61.81%), last year (62.07%) and peers. No measurable revenue effect.

findings.title: Customers don't recognise the brand and doubt it is legitimate (new market, marketing can address)
findings.evidence: trust_brand is 33 of 228 comments (14.5%) vs 2.9% elsewhere and 6.6% before. Gist: 'never heard of the brand, doubts legitimacy'. CPA is €27.09 vs a peer range of €20.7–21.7. In week 32 after launch, revenue/day is €36,509, 44% of what São Paulo had at the same age. This is a brand-awareness issue, not a defect.

proposed_actions.action: Open a P1 ticket with payments/engineering for the iOS checkout (card declines and failures) in Paris and Madrid, starting 2026-10-14. Check the iOS payment SDK/3DS or the release shipped that day. Use Android as the control.
proposed_actions.why: About €1.39M a month is being lost across both markets. Marketing can't fix it, and every euro spent on ads that sends iOS traffic there is partly wasted.

proposed_actions.action: Until the fix ships, send recovery emails/SMS to iOS users who abandoned checkout in Paris and Madrid since 2026-10-14, with a desktop or alternative-payment link.
proposed_actions.why: About 37.9k iOS checkouts across the two markets ended without an order. Some of that revenue can be won back.

proposed_actions.action: Send a ticket to ops/logistics about the Berlin carrier delays (since week 40), and send affected Berlin customers a proactive apology and delivery-status email.
proposed_actions.why: NPS fell from -10 to -48 and repeat share is 3.9 points below peers. This will keep costing retention.

proposed_actions.action: Lifecycle email: run a back-in-stock/waitlist flow for PAR-GFT-E10 (Paris · Gifts · Edition 11, €66, sold out 2026-10-23). In Amsterdam Gifts, send new-gift-range announcement emails (8 of 61 comments, 13.1%, ask for more gift options).
proposed_actions.why: There is demand we couldn't fill. praise_product is the most common theme overall (568 mentions, 21% of comments), so happy customers can be targeted for reviews and referrals.

proposed_actions.action: In Miami, add trust signals (reviews, press, guarantees) to ads and landing pages.
proposed_actions.why: Comments doubting the brand's legitimacy have doubled, and CPA is above peers.

not_problems: Comment data has no product_id, so mentions can only be tied to market × line, not to individual products. The only product-level signal is the PAR-GFT-E10 sell-out.

Across all markets, theme volumes are stable compared with the prior 28 days: praise_product 568 vs 556, price_value 327 vs 331, product_quality 189 vs 210, returns_refunds 124 vs 125. No network-wide product-defect or returns spike.
sold_out complaints fell overall (91 vs 113).
Milan's navigation complaints don't show up in conversion: checkout→order matches last year and peers.
Berlin revenue/day is in line with last year and above peers. The delivery problem shows in NPS and repeat share, not yet in current sales.
NPS improved in London (-23 to -5), Mexico City (-23 to 2), New York and Amsterdam. Barcelona and São Paulo are flat. Nothing to act on there.

output.summary: Moving spend between channels inside each line's existing budget is worth about €149k/week in revenue (≈€644k/month) for the 19 market-lines whose plans I could read. Only €41k/week (≈€179k/month) of that comes from lines where the model fits well on a full 60 weeks of data, so treat the rest as something to test, not a forecast. The pattern is the same in nearly every market-line: Google brand search and Meta retargeting bring in little extra revenue per euro (Google brand €0.02–0.87 back per €1) and can fund YouTube, TikTok and creators (€2.4–10 per €1). London overspent its October budget by €66.5k (+18.5%), and Paris and Madrid organic revenue is down about 20% on last year even though search demand is flat. That organic drop is a real problem, not seasonality.

findings.title: Portfolio channel shift inside each line: +€148.8k/week of revenue expected (19 market-lines visible)
findings.evidence: The plan's tool output was cut off after 19 of 44 market-lines. Their expected weekly gains add up to €148,820 (≈€644k/month at 4.33 weeks), or +3.8% to +7.3% per line. The 25 lines I could not see each gain ≤€5,436/week, the smallest gain shown. Only revenue can be sized; I did not pull margin data, so the gross-profit uplift is not stated. Of the €148.8k: €41.3k/week (≈€179k/month) comes from 5 lines with r2 ≥0.7 on 60 weeks: New York Home €10,714 (r2 0.726), New York Gifts €9,636 (0.909), London Gifts €8,393 (0.924), Barcelona Home €7,115 (0.754), Berlin Gifts €5,436 (0.919). €23.1k/week comes from São Paulo (r2 0.98+ but only 42 weeks). €19.3k/week comes from poor fits: Paris Beauty €7,352 (r2 0.282), Paris Fashion drops €6,299 (0.243), Milan Fashion drops €5,690 (0.362). The plan breaks its own stated ±50% channel limit, with increases of +60% to +84%, so the stated gains are probably too high.

findings.title: Model fit: good in 23 of 44 market-lines, but only 15 of those have a full history
findings.evidence: r2 ≥0.7 in 23 of 44 market-lines. Gifts is good in all 11 markets with a model (0.607 Paris, 0.851–0.944 elsewhere). Amsterdam is good in all 4 lines (0.74–0.944). São Paulo (0.983–0.989, 42 weeks) and Miami (0.989–0.992, 32 weeks) fit almost perfectly, which with 8 channels plus search as inputs on so few weeks looks like overfitting. r2 is below 0.5 in 6 lines: Paris Fashion drops 0.243, Paris Beauty 0.282, Madrid Fashion drops 0.312, Madrid Beauty 0.323, Milan Fashion drops 0.362, Berlin Beauty 0.424. Mexico City has no model (8 weeks of data). Search interest explains most of the revenue (search elasticity ≈0.95 everywhere). The all-market Meta prospecting figure (0.9524) equals that search figure, so it reflects demand and should not be trusted; per-line Meta prospecting is 0.06–0.08. Ask the model owner for MAPE: the tool reports only r2.

findings.title: Google brand search is saturated: it gets most of the last-click credit but brings in little extra revenue
findings.evidence: Last 28 days: €408,524 spent. Our own last-click data says 9.48 ROAS and the platform claims 10.4, but the model's return on the next euro is only 0.02 (Paris Gifts) to 0.87 (São Paulo Home). Most lines are below 0.5, for example London Home 0.13, Barcelona Beauty 0.06 and Amsterdam Fashion drops 0.03. The plan cuts brand search by 39–47% in every line it shows.

findings.title: Meta retargeting: platform claims about twice what our own data shows, and the model says it adds little
findings.evidence: Platform ROAS 3.47 against 1.59 from our own last-click data (€1.22M claimed vs €559k last-click on €351k spend over 28 days). The model's return on the next euro is mostly below 1, e.g. London Beauty 0.44, Madrid Beauty 0.36, Berlin Gifts 0.46. Exceptions are São Paulo (1.63–2.11) and Paris Home (1.89). TikTok also over-claims (platform 6.04 vs our 3.38), but the model still values its next euro at 1.72–7.54.

findings.title: YouTube, TikTok and creators are under-funded in every market
findings.evidence: YouTube's return on the next euro is 2.41–9.98 on only €611–1,559/week per line (London Home 8.09, New York Home 8.72, São Paulo Home 9.98). TikTok is 1.72–7.54 and creators 1.42–7.52. Our last-click data undercounts YouTube (2.98 ROAS vs the platform's 5.73), as expected for upper-funnel video.

findings.title: Moving budget between lines: Beauty earns least per extra euro, Home and New York/São Paulo lines earn most
findings.evidence: Blended return on the next euro, top lines: São Paulo Home 3.71, New York Home 2.73, São Paulo Fashion drops 2.73, São Paulo Gifts 2.72, New York Fashion drops 2.51, London Home 2.43, Paris Home 2.32. Bottom: Amsterdam Beauty 0.79 (€13,386/week), Madrid Beauty 0.98 (€15,253/week), Miami Beauty 1.00, Amsterdam Fashion drops 1.05, Lisbon Beauty 1.09, Milan Beauty 1.12. These are marginal returns at the current spend level, so large moves should be stepped and re-checked.

findings.title: London overspent its October budget by €66.5k (+18.5%); Milan by €22k
findings.evidence: October spend €426,549 against a €360,000 budget; September was on plan at €357,657. Milan spent €274,205 against €252,000 (+8.8%). Organic-vs-paid shows London's 28-day spend up 6.8% while paid revenue rose only 0.7%. November pacing (projected at 90.9%) rests on 1 day of data and is not yet meaningful.

findings.title: Organic revenue in Paris and Madrid is down about 20% on last year while search demand is flat
findings.evidence: Organic revenue vs last year: Paris −24.3% and Madrid −20.2%, with spend roughly flat (−2.0% and −1.7%). Search interest over the last 4 weeks vs last year: Paris +0.3%, Madrid −0.4%. So falling demand does not explain it; the cause is likely conversion, site or stock problems. Milan organic is −18.2% on last year with search −2.5%.

findings.title: Mexico City and Miami are well under budget
findings.evidence: October: Mexico City spent €134,634 of €260,000 (it started in September and spent €38,200 then). Miami spent €196,104 of €264,000. November projections are 63.6% and 81.8%, though these rest on 1 day of data. Mexico City has no model to judge whether more spend would pay off.

proposed_actions.action: Apply the channel shift first in the 5 well-fitted, full-history lines (New York Home, New York Gifts, London Gifts, Barcelona Home, Berlin Gifts). Cap each channel at ±50% of current spend, and at ±30% in the first month. Example for London Home: Google brand €3,143→€1,710/week, Meta retargeting €2,977→€1,619/week, moved into YouTube, TikTok and creators.
proposed_actions.why: The model expects €41.3k/week of revenue (≈€179k/month) from these lines, and r2 is 0.73–0.92 there. The uncapped plan's moves of +60% to +84% go beyond where the model has data and break its own ±50% limit.

proposed_actions.action: In poorly fitted lines (Paris Fashion drops and Beauty, Madrid Fashion drops and Beauty, Milan Fashion drops, Berlin Beauty) and in São Paulo and Miami, run the shift as a geo or holdout test rather than a full rollout.
proposed_actions.why: r2 is 0.24–0.42 in the first group. São Paulo and Miami have r2 ≈0.99 on only 32–42 weeks, which suggests overfitting, so their expected gains could easily be off by 50% or more.

proposed_actions.action: Run an incrementality test on Google brand search: pause or cut it about 40% in 2–3 markets for 4 weeks.
proposed_actions.why: It looks like a 9.48 ROAS on last click, but the model says the next euro returns 0.02–0.87. This is the largest single funding source for the shift.

proposed_actions.action: Hold London to its €360k budget in November and put the overspend into YouTube or TikTok, not retargeting or brand search.
proposed_actions.why: London went €66.5k over budget in October, and in London Home the next euro returns 0.13 on brand search vs 8.09 on YouTube.

proposed_actions.action: Move €10–20k/month of Beauty budget (Amsterdam, Madrid, Lisbon) into Home lines in New York, London and São Paulo, in steps.
proposed_actions.why: The blended return on the next euro is 0.79–1.09 in those Beauty lines vs 2.43–3.71 in the Home lines.

proposed_actions.action: Look into the cause of the Paris and Madrid organic drop (conversion rate, stock-outs, site issues) before adding paid spend there.
proposed_actions.why: Organic is about 20% below last year while search demand is flat, so this is not seasonality.

proposed_actions.action: Release unspent Mexico City and Miami budget only against a ramp plan; otherwise reallocate it to the top lines by return on the next euro.
proposed_actions.why: Together they were €193k under budget in October, and Mexico City has no model yet.
